title: Listen smart: arguments and intentions
objective: Identifier arguments et intentions dans une présentation courte

steps.title: Warm-up: your best study tip
steps.student_instruction: Share your best tip for exams with a partner. Is it advice, a warning or information?
steps.facilitator_instruction: Introduire to advise / to warn / to inform / to persuade à partir des exemples des élèves.

steps.title: Listening: Advice for exams
steps.student_instruction: Listen to the teacher's talk. Take notes with key words and symbols.
steps.facilitator_instruction: Faire écouter l'audio British Council (QR code) ; sans réseau, lire le script de secours. Première écoute : intention générale ; seconde : arguments et raisons.

steps.title: Language focus: notes and intentions
steps.student_instruction: Learn note-taking symbols and the language of advice, reasons and warnings.
steps.facilitator_instruction: Symboles (+, ->, x, =) ; should / don't / try to ; because / so ; distinguer argument et exemple.

steps.title: Differentiated practice
steps.student_instruction: Complete your A, B or C sheet with the model talk.
steps.facilitator_instruction: A : grille à compléter ; B : notes libres puis reformulation ; C : analyse de l'intention et de l'efficacité des arguments.

steps.title: Talk and report
steps.student_instruction: Listen to a classmate's one-minute advice talk. Note the intention, three arguments and one example, then report back.
steps.facilitator_instruction: Groupes de 3 ; un orateur, deux preneurs de notes ; comparer les notes avant de restituer.

steps.title: Exit ticket
steps.student_instruction: Write the intention of today's talk and its strongest argument.
steps.facilitator_instruction: Ramasser ; vérifier la distinction argument / intention.

sheets.student_content: Complete the notes grid for Mr Hall's talk: intention (inform / warn / persuade?), argument 1: ___, argument 2: ___, advice: ___.
sheets.facilitator_correction: Intention : to persuade ; argument 1 : teenagers need about nine hours of sleep ; argument 2 : sleep helps memory ; advice : switch off your phone one hour before bed.

sheets.student_content: Take notes on the exam talk with symbols. Then write four sentences reporting the teacher's advice (She advises... / She says that...).
sheets.facilitator_correction: Exemple : She advises us to eat apples. She says we should take a five-minute break every half hour. She warns us not to drink cola.

sheets.student_content: Which argument in the exam talk is the most convincing? Explain in 100 words, and suggest one argument the teacher forgot.
sheets.facilitator_correction: Production libre ; critères : argument identifié, justification, argument nouveau pertinent.

criteria: L'élève relève au moins deux arguments
